note: Reviewed starting links from economic drivers, in India and worldwide ('region'; Indian when absent), to the eight shares. Every link is INFERRED: it says a driver may affect a share, never the direction or size. Edit with care; chains.py study tests whether each link carries information.

links.basis: Refining and petrochemicals are a large part of the business; crude prices move margins and inventory values.
Telecom and retail subsidiaries are large earnings contributors.
Policy rates change lending margins, deposit costs and credit growth.
System-wide loan quality and growth data move all large lenders.
Most revenue is earned in foreign currency and reported in rupees.
Client technology budgets and peer results signal demand.
Cigarettes are the largest profit pool and taxes set their volumes and pricing.
Generation volumes, plant load and fuel availability drive earnings.
Market-wide flows and index moves affect every large constituent.
US rates move foreign money into or out of Indian banks and set the dollar, which converts Infosys's revenue.
Major central banks set global liquidity, which moves foreign flows into large Indian shares.
US and European clients' technology budgets drive most of the demand for Indian IT services.
Supply shocks and sanctions move crude prices and refining margins.
Chinese demand sets world prices for petrochemicals and coal.
Imported coal prices feed generation costs.
Tariffs change export demand, input costs and the rupee.
Global risk appetite moves foreign flows into and out of emerging-market large caps.
